gates.reason: The authenticated push-ingest path securely contains artifact destinations, but its metadata and signature-ledger writes do not verify that .sources/<sourceId> remains inside the configured ingest root after symlink resolution.

Inspected recommendation/audit projections, arithmetic aggregation, cache provenance gates, stale-guidance relabeling, and validated-fix response paths; no reproducible integrity defect survived review.
Large uncached live bodies are compressed synchronously on the main event loop for every request, despite allowing raw responses up to tens or hundreds of MiB.

findings.title: Push-ingest metadata writes can follow a symlink outside the ingest root
findings.what: The handler validates and opens each artifact destination with realpath containment and O_NOFOLLOW, but writes _source.json and .signatures.json through metaRoot using plain writeFile. If the pre-existing .sources directory or .sources/<sourceId> is a symlink, these authenticated writes follow it and overwrite files outside PROBAITIO_INGEST_DIR. sourceId validation prevents textual traversal but does not prevent this filesystem traversal.
findings.fix: Resolve and verify the canonical .sources and per-source metadata directories beneath realIngest before use, reject symlinks, and write both files through descriptor-bound O_NOFOLLOW opens with restrictive permissions.
findings.acceptance: Create an ingest root whose .sources or .sources/<valid-source-id> is a symlink to an external directory, submit an otherwise valid authenticated batch, and verify the request is rejected and neither _source.json nor .signatures.json is created or changed outside the ingest root; verify normal metadata writes still succeed in a real contained directory.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed that artifact writes receive canonical-parent containment plus O_NOFOLLOW at scripts/server.mjs:5753-5778, while the two metadata writes at 5787 and 5793 use writeFile directly and have no equivalent canonical containment or no-follow check.

findings.title: Per-request synchronous compression can block the server event loop on large live responses
findings.what: sendBody negotiates Brotli or gzip by calling brotliCompressSync/gzipSync on the request thread whenever no precompressed body is supplied. Raw history and merged-session routes pass potentially very large bodies through this path, so each requesting client can repeatedly monopolize the single Node.js event loop and delay all concurrent requests.
findings.fix: Make live-body compression asynchronous or stream it through zlib transforms; alternatively decline dynamic compression above a small fixed threshold and send the body uncompressed. Preserve the existing precompressed dataset path.
findings.acceptance: Request a near-limit history or merged-session response with Accept-Encoding: br and concurrently poll a lightweight endpoint; verify compression no longer causes event-loop latency spikes beyond the documented request budget, and verify Content-Encoding/body correctness for Brotli, gzip, and identity clients.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed that the cached dataset supplies precompressed buffers, but generic live/raw routes do not; sendBody therefore executes the synchronous Brotli or gzip branches once per encoded request with no body-size threshold.
